relatedSnapshot.title: Domain migration: <domain> → app.acquisity.ai
relatedSnapshot.description:
Rename production hosts from `<domain>` to `acquisity.ai`. Existing user sessions will be logged out at cutover (cookies are tied to the host). Plan: run both domains side by side for at least a month, then retire the old one.

## Decisions to lock before starting

- [ ] Name 2 OAuth: wait 4–6 weeks for Name 2 to verify the new domain (safer), or build a small bridge so the cutover does not block on Name 2 review?
- [ ] FeatureBase tenant `aiacquisition` (used for the in-app feedback widget): keep the slug or rename it?
- [ ] Visual rebrand: are we shipping new logo / favicon / OAuth consent-screen assets at the same time, or keeping the existing visuals and only changing the host?

## DNS and Vercel

- [ ] Set up the Cloudflare zone for `acquisity.ai`
- [ ] Add DNS records: `app`, `*.app`, `oauth-proxy`, `assets`, `dev-assets`, `images`, `<domain>`, `info`, `go`
- [ ] Keep records DNS-only at first, no Cloudflare proxy on the app/wildcard ones, until certs are issued
- [ ] If Cloudflare stays authoritative, add the `_acme-challenge` delegation record Vercel asks for so the wildcard cert can issue
- [ ] Add the new domains to the Vercel project: `app.acquisity.ai` and the `*.app.acquisity.ai` wildcard
- [ ] Confirm TLS is green on every new domain (curl)
- [ ] Update Vercel env vars for production: `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL`, `OAUTH_PROXY_URL` (preview only), `NEXT_PUBLIC_ASSETS_CDN_URL`, `CLOUDFLARE_TRANSFORM_ZONE_URL`, `S3_DOCS_PUBLIC_URL`, `EMAIL_FROM`, `SUPPORT_EMAIL`
- [ ] Do NOT touch `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, OAuth client secrets, Inngest signing keys, database URLs, or R2 bucket names — rotating these creates extra outage risk

## Email and sending domain

- [ ] Add `info.acquisity.ai` in Resend, publish DKIM/SPF/DMARC TXT records
- [ ] Start DMARC at `p=quarantine` and watch reports for two weeks before tightening
- [ ] Ramp send volume on the new domain gradually (transactional first, announcements last)
- [ ] Keep the old SPF/DKIM/DMARC live until the new domain has at least 14 days of clean delivery

## Brand assets (logo, favicon, OAuth consent-screen)

Most asset work is independent of the host migration — the bundled files (`public/images/ai-clients-logo.svg`, `app/favicon.svg`, `app/favicon.ico`, `app/apple-icon.png`, `public/images/android-chrome-192x192.png`) are served from whatever origin the app runs on, so they follow the host automatically. The work below is only required if we are also refreshing the visual identity, plus the items that are always required because R2-hosted assets sit behind a separate custom domain.

- [ ] Decide whether the rebrand includes new logo / favicon / app-icon files. If yes, drop replacements into `public/images/` and `app/` (same filenames keep cache behavior simple)
- [ ] Name 3 for `ai-clients-logo` and confirm any direct references still resolve
- [ ] If the visual logo is changing: upload the new logo to the Name 2 OAuth consent screen and Microsoft Name 4 app branding. Note that re-uploading the OAuth consent-screen logo is one of the changes that triggers Name 2 brand re-verification — bundle this into the same Name 2 submission as the new authorized domain, so we only go through one review cycle
- [ ] Update Stripe public business profile logo (statement descriptor uses a separate "icon" upload), Slack OAuth app icon if applicable, Intercom messenger logo, FeatureBase workspace logo, Sentry/PostHog org icons (low priority — only visible to internal users)
- [ ] R2-hosted partner-uploaded logos (`partner.logoUrl`) follow the R2 custom-domain dual-attach already in the next section — no DB rewrite needed, but verify a partner with a real uploaded logo still renders after `assets.acquisity.ai` is attached
- [ ] Re-run the docs screenshot tool if hero images in `content/docs/**/*.mdx` show the old logo prominently (or accept stale images and refresh later)

## External providers (add new URLs alongside the old, do not remove yet)

- [ ] Name 2 OAuth: file verification with `acquisity.ai` added; reuse the same client ID; add new authorized origins and redirect URIs (sign-in callback, Gmail integration callback, OAuth proxy URL for the preview client)
- [ ] Microsoft Name 4: add new redirect URIs to prod and preview clients; add publisher-domain TXT to the new apex while keeping the old TXT
- [ ] Autumn / Stripe billing: add a new endpoint, capture its signing secret, do not flip primary yet
- [ ] Whop platform app: add a new redirect URI and webhook subscription
- [ ] PayPal: new return URLs and webhook URL, generate new `PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ID`
- [ ] <domain>: new bot and recording webhook URLs
- [ ] Twilio: update the TwiML Name 5 URLs (Voice, Voice Fallback, Status Callback, SMS), audit per-phone-number overrides, update the Messaging Service inbound webhook
- [ ] Inngest: confirm app endpoint URL after deploy (Vercel auto-syncs on deploy if the integration is installed)
- [ ] PostHog: add new domains to project Authorized Domains
- [ ] Sentry: add new domains to project Allowed Domains (allow 24h to propagate)
- [ ] FeatureBase IDV, Intercom messenger, Pipedream allowed origins, Name 6 redirect URLs, Zoom Video redirect URI, Name 7 endpoint
- [ ] Calendly: confirm whether direct subscriptions exist (vs Pipedream); update only the ones we own
- [ ] R2 CORS: add new origins to every browser-upload bucket and confirm with a real upload from a Vercel preview
- [ ] R2 custom domains: attach the new ones (`docs-images.app.acquisity.ai`, `assets.acquisity.ai`, `dev-assets.acquisity.ai`) alongside the old; do not remove old yet

## Code changes

- [ ] New shared module `lib/platform-domains.ts` that holds every platform host as a constant, with helpers `isKnownPlatformHost`, `extractPartnerSlug`, and partner-subdomain regex patterns covering both old and new roots
- [ ] Extend `lib/auth/team-config.ts` to accept `acquisity.ai` and add an `isTeamEmail()` helper. Keep `<domain>` in the list during transition
- [ ] Refactor the eight inline `endsWith(<email>')` call sites (auth/index, nps router, preview-whop-testing, preview-list route, calendly client, onboarding seeding, internal-team-webhook, submission seed data) to use `isTeamEmail`. This is a hard prerequisite for the OAuth bridge option
- [ ] Update routing/auth core constants in `lib/get-base-url.ts`, `lib/partner/subdomain.ts`, `lib/partner/resolve-edge.ts`, `lib/partner/resolve.ts`, `proxy.ts`, `app.config.ts`, `next.config.ts` to import from the new module
- [ ] Update email defaults: `lib/email/service.ts`, `lib/email/services/announcement-email.ts`, `lib/theming/app-branding.ts`, `trpc/routers/partner-admin.ts`, `app/(saas)/dashboard/(sidebar)/partner-admin/emails/page.tsx`
- [ ] Update user-facing UI copy: sign-in card, sign-up booking link, subscription-gate docs URLs, ai-website-creator publish flow
- [ ] In `trpc/routers/admin/admin-partners.ts`, replace the inline `<domain>` literal with the existing `getPartnerSubdomainForEnvironment()` helper. The plan earlier called this a "stored column" — it is not, it is computed
- [ ] Centralize bootstrap-user lookup behind a `BOOTSTRAP_SYSTEM_USER_EMAIL` env var; refactor the four webhook handlers that hard-code `<email>`
- [ ] Update n8n workflow template names and the email-template Storybook preview URL
- [ ] If the OAuth bridge option is chosen: add a new `OAUTH_CALLBACK_HOST_OVERRIDE` env var, expose `getCanonicalOAuthHost()`, route `lib/oauth/proxy-utils.ts` through it
- [ ] Update test fixtures, add assertions that legacy hosts still resolve during transition and that both team domains are accepted
- [ ] Update the docs MDX hero-image hostnames (or add a Cloudflare rewrite from the old image host to the new)
- [ ] Update `.env.example`
- [ ] `bun typecheck`, `bun test:unit` for touched modules, `bun lint:mdx` if docs changed, `bun ci`

## Cutover

- [ ] Re-confirm: TLS green on all new domains, Name 2 verified or bridge built, Resend warmed up, R2 CORS updated, every external provider has received a successful test event on the new host, on-call staffed
- [ ] Quiet/pause high-volume scheduled jobs that could flood queues during rollback
- [ ] Merge and deploy the code PR to production
- [ ] Sanity-check the new domains directly with curl
- [ ] In Vercel: assign `app.acquisity.ai` as primary production domain
- [ ] Trigger Inngest re-sync (re-deploy if needed)
- [ ] Flip provider dashboards to "new is primary, old still enabled": Autumn/Stripe, Whop, Recall, PayPal, Twilio, Calendly/Pipedream if active, Resend, Name 7
- [ ] Enable a 308 redirect from `<domain>/*` to the new host. 308 preserves POST bodies and query strings, which matters for OAuth callbacks and webhook replays. Do this at one layer only (Vercel project-level redirect) to avoid double-hop chains
- [ ] Verify the redirect: GET `/dashboard`, GET an OAuth callback URL with `code` and `state`, POST a test webhook and confirm method and body survive
- [ ] Smoke-test from a clean browser: sign in (Name 2, Microsoft, email/password, 2FA), accept an org invite, connect Gmail and Outlook, trigger a billing test event, trigger Whop/Recall/PayPal/Twilio/Inngest/Athena test events, upload to each R2 bucket category, send a transactional email, open docs images, hit a partner subdomain and confirm branding (including a partner with an uploaded logo)

## Rollback safety net (do not violate)

- [ ] Old Vercel domain attachment stays for at least 30 days
- [ ] Old origins stay in R2 CORS for at least 30 days
- [ ] Old redirect URIs stay in Name 2 and Microsoft OAuth for at least 30 days
- [ ] Old DNS records stay for at least 90 days
- [ ] `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, OAuth client secrets, Inngest signing keys never rotated as part of this migration
- [ ] `<domain>` registrar set to auto-renew indefinitely. Abandoned auth domains are a phishing risk

relatedSnapshot.title: Lead Magnet campaigns
relatedSnapshot.description:
# Build AI SDR Lead Magnet campaigns

## Objective

Build Lead Magnet campaigns for AI SDR so a campaign can send a configured resource when a prospect replies with interest but does not book immediately.

The MVP should be safe to merge in pieces before release. Most work should be built behind hidden campaign-type plumbing. The final release step is only adding Lead Magnet to the Campaign Type dropdown.

## Updated MVP Flow

 1. User opens a campaign.
 2. User selects Campaign Type: Lead Magnet.
 3. A Lead Magnet resource block appears directly under Campaign Type in the campaign Options tab.
 4. User uploads a resource file or pastes an approved external video link.
 5. Uploaded files are hosted by Acquisity as Hosted Resources.
 6. External video links are stored as Hosted Resources pointing to the external URL.
 7. User describes the resource in a free-text context field so the AI SDR understands what it is sending.
 8. Campaign cannot go active unless a Lead Magnet resource is linked.
 9. AI SDR receives a positive non-booking reply on a Lead Magnet campaign.
10. AI SDR sends the linked resource URL, using the resource context to write a coherent reply.
11. AI SDR schedules Lead Magnet-specific follow-ups using the existing follow-up system with Lead Magnet-specific timing and prompts.
12. Explicit booking intent still routes to booking, booking the call type configured in the Lead Magnet Method settings.
13. Duplicating a Lead Magnet campaign copies the linked resources independently.

## Required Product Decisions

### Release Strategy

Lead Magnet must not be selectable until the final release ticket.

Tickets before release should be safe to merge because:

* `lead-magnet` exists only as hidden internal campaign type plumbing.
* Hosted Resources can exist without being exposed to Lead Magnet users.
* Campaign resource UI only appears when a campaign is already `lead-magnet`.
* AI SDR Lead Magnet behavior only runs when campaign type is `lead-magnet`.
* The final ticket only adds Lead Magnet to the Campaign Type dropdown.

### Hosted Resources

Lead Magnet resources should use a new shared model called Hosted Resources.

Hosted Resources are not campaign-specific. They are organization-owned resources that campaigns, workflows, and future product surfaces can use.

Campaigns should expose linked resources as:

```ts
campaign.resources
```

The database should use a reusable resource table and a campaign link table, likely:

* `hosted_resource`
* `outreach_campaign_hosted_resource`

MVP uses one Lead Magnet resource per campaign, but the campaign API should use an array so multiple resources can be supported later.

Each resource carries a free-text context/description field and is served via a stable, public, non-expiring URL built on a random, unguessable token (no signed URLs, not enumerable across organizations).

### Resource Types

MVP supports:

* Uploaded files: PDF, PNG, JPG, JPEG.
* External video links: approved HTTPS video hosts such as Loom, YouTube, or Name 8.

Uploaded files should be hosted by Acquisity. Pasted links that point to hostable file types should be rejected and the user should be prompted to upload the file instead.

### AI SDR Behavior

Lead Magnet behavior should be handled by AI SDR routing and a new send-resource step/agent.

The step should receive the linked resource URL directly and include it in the reply. It also receives the resource's free-text context/description so the reply (and follow-ups) speak to what is being sent rather than emitting a blind URL.

No general-purpose `{{magnet}}` merge variable is required for MVP.

Booking intent always wins. When a Lead Magnet campaign routes to booking, it books the call type configured in the Lead Magnet Method settings. Existing question, objection, negative, out-of-office, wrong-person, referral, and platform-switch routes should stay unchanged.

### Follow-ups

Lead Magnet follow-ups should reuse the existing follow-up system, but with Lead Magnet-specific timing and prompts.

Follow-ups should not claim the prospect opened or read the resource.

## MVP Includes

* Hidden Lead Magnet campaign type plumbing.
* Shared Hosted Resources schema and independent API.
* Campaign-to-Hosted-Resource linking.
* `campaign.resources` read shape.
* Free-text lead magnet context field on the resource (manual entry).
* Stable public resource URLs using random, unguessable tokens.
* Upload validation for PDF, PNG, JPG, and JPEG.
* External video link validation.
* Hidden campaign Options resource block.
* Activation guard requiring a resource for Lead Magnet campaigns.
* Active-campaign remove-resource pause flow.
* Campaign duplication support for linked Hosted Resources (including context).
* AI SDR Lead Magnet intent routing.
* AI SDR send-resource step/agent (context-aware).
* Lead Magnet Method settings block (call type to book + follow-up delay defaults).
* Lead Magnet-specific follow-up timing and prompts.
* Final dropdown exposure.

## Out of Scope

* Resource analytics.
* Shared Resource Center UI.
* Dynamic per-lead landing pages.
* Multi-resource Lead Magnet campaign UX.
* General-purpose `{{magnet}}` merge variable support — including the client placing a token in their own sequence copy (e.g. the breakup email to non-repliers). Deliberately cut for v1.
* LLM auto-summary of an uploaded resource into the context field (V2; manual entry only for now).
* Text extraction from uploaded resources.
* External link wrapping or click tracking.
* Auto-pause notification — platform-wide gap, deferred; not Lead Magnet-specific.
* Changes to the existing AI SDR Resources settings section (still used by other campaign types; left untouched).
* Campaign type detector support unless separately approved.

## Recommended Build Order

Use this sequence for implementation planning. Name 9's child issue ordering does not need to reflect dependency/build order.

1. ENG-9967
2. ENG-9968
3. ENG-9969
4. ENG-9970
5. ENG-9971
6. ENG-10234
7. ENG-9972
8. ENG-9973
9. ENG-9974

## Security Requirements

* Hosted Resources must be organization-scoped.
* Users must not be able to link resources across organizations.
* Upload URLs, storage keys, and signed URLs must not leak secrets to logs.
* Public resource URLs must use random, unguessable tokens and must not be enumerable across organizations.
* Hosted Resource APIs must enforce organization membership.
* Campaign-resource links must validate that campaign and resource belong to the same organization.
* File validation must happen server-side.

## Acceptance Criteria

* Lead Magnet remains hidden until the final release ticket.
* Lead Magnet can be represented internally as a campaign method.
* Hosted Resources can be created independently from campaigns.
* Campaign reads expose linked resources as `campaign.resources`.
* Users can upload PDF, PNG, JPG, and JPEG Hosted Resources.
* Users can create Hosted Resources from approved external video links.
* Users can add a free-text context description for a Lead Magnet resource.
* A Lead Magnet campaign cannot go active without a linked resource.
* Removing a resource from an active Lead Magnet campaign pauses the campaign after warning.
* Duplicated Lead Magnet campaigns receive independent resource copies, including context.
* AI SDR sends the linked resource for positive non-booking replies on Lead Magnet campaigns, using the resource context.
* Explicit booking intent still routes to booking, using the configured Lead Magnet Method call type.
* Lead Magnet resource sends schedule Lead Magnet-specific follow-ups.
* Existing campaign types and AI SDR routes remain unchanged.
* The final release ticket only exposes Lead Magnet in the Campaign Type dropdown.

## Resolved Review Decisions (2026-06-15)

* **Lead magnet context for the AI SDR:** add a manual free-text context field on the resource for v1, threaded into the send-resource and follow-up prompts. LLM auto-summary from the file is future work (V2). → ENG-9968 (storage), ENG-9970 (UI), ENG-9972/ENG-9973 (prompts).
* **Lead Magnet Method block:** add a configurable Lead Magnet method with the call type to book and follow-up delay defaults. → ENG-10234, consumed by ENG-9972/ENG-9973.
* **Prospect-facing URL:** stable public URL (no signed URLs), with a random, unguessable token in the path and inline rendering; not enumerable across orgs. → ENG-9968/ENG-9969.
* `{{magnet}}` **token:** cut for v1, including the client-placed-in-own-copy / breakup-email use case. Deliberate scope decision.
* **Auto-pause notification:** deferred as a platform-wide concern, out of scope here.
* **Old AI SDR Resources section:** left untouched (still used by other campaign types).
* **Shared resource API/architecture:** intentionally kept; the shared Hosted Resources model is built now to support future dynamic resources via workflows (related ENG-10002).

## Notes For Child Tickets

Each child ticket should include its own focused tests. Do not create a separate testing-only child ticket.

Completed child tickets should not be rewritten if product scope shifts. Track implementation deltas as follow-up child tickets instead.

## Sub-issues

* Hidden Lead Magnet campaign type plumbing
* Shared Hosted Resources schema + independent API
* Hosted Resources upload + external link validation
* Hidden Lead Magnet resource UI + campaign guards
* Campaign duplication copies linked resources
* Lead Magnet Method settings block (call type + follow-up delay)
* AI SDR Lead Magnet intent routing + send-resource step
* Lead Magnet-specific follow-up behavior
* Release Lead Magnet campaign type

relatedSnapshot.title: Hosted Resources upload + external link validation
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Objective

Add concrete Hosted Resource creation paths for uploaded files and approved external video links.

Lead Magnet campaigns need both uploaded PDFs/images hosted by Acquisity and external video links such as Loom, YouTube, or Name 8.

## Scope

* Support uploaded resources for PDF, PNG, JPG, and JPEG.
* Enforce the agreed file size cap, likely 25 MB.
* Persist uploaded file metadata on `hosted_resource`.
* Store uploaded files through the platform's existing storage layer.
* Serve uploaded files at their stable public token URL (defined in ENG-9968) with inline content disposition so they render in the browser instead of force-downloading. No signed URLs.
* Support approved HTTPS video URLs.
* Reject malformed URLs.
* Reject unsupported hosts.
* Reject pasted URLs that appear to point to hostable files, such as `.pdf`, `.png`, `.jpg`, or `.jpeg`, with guidance to upload the file instead.
* Do not extract text from uploaded resources.

## Acceptance Criteria

* Users can create a Hosted Resource from a valid PDF, PNG, JPG, or JPEG upload.
* Uploaded files over the size cap are rejected.
* Unsupported uploaded file types are rejected.
* Uploaded files render inline in the browser at their stable public token URL (not force-downloaded, not a signed/expiring URL).
* Users can create a Hosted Resource from an approved HTTPS video URL.
* Malformed and unsupported URLs are rejected.
* Hostable file URLs are rejected from the pasted-link path.
* Hosted Resource records include enough metadata to render name, type, and URL in later UI.
* Focused tests cover accepted uploads, rejected uploads, file size limit, inline serving, accepted video URLs, malformed URLs, unsupported URLs, and hostable file URL rejection.

relatedSnapshot.title: Hidden Lead Magnet resource UI + campaign guards
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Objective

Build the campaign Options resource setup experience and enforcement rules for Lead Magnet campaigns while keeping the feature hidden from normal users.

Lead Magnet is still not selectable at this point, so this work should be safe to merge before release.

## Scope

* Add a resource block under Campaign Type in the campaign Options tab.
* Render the block only when the campaign method is already `lead-magnet`.
* Bind the UI to `campaign.resources`.
* Support Upload file and Paste link modes.
* Support replacing the linked resource.
* Support removing the linked resource.
* Add a free-text "Lead magnet context" field in the resource block where the campaign builder describes the asset (what it is, how to use it, likely questions/objections) for the AI SDR. Manual entry for v1, bound to the linked resource. (LLM-generated "Generate summary from the uploaded document" button is future work / V2 and out of scope here.)
* Show helper text explaining what the resource is for and what the context field is used for.
* Block activating a Lead Magnet campaign without a linked resource.
* If a resource is removed from an active Lead Magnet campaign, warn the user and pause the campaign if confirmed.
* Store a clear pause reason, such as `resource_missing`.
* Do not add Lead Magnet to any dropdown in this ticket.

## Acceptance Criteria

* A Lead Magnet campaign shows a resource block under Campaign Type.
* Non-Lead-Magnet campaigns do not show the resource block.
* The resource block supports upload and external link modes.
* The resource block displays the currently linked resource.
* The resource block includes a free-text lead magnet context field, persisted on the linked resource.
* Replacing the resource updates the linked Hosted Resource and does not pause an active campaign.
* Removing a resource from a draft or paused campaign unlinks it without active-campaign side effects.
* Removing a resource from an active Lead Magnet campaign warns first and pauses the campaign if confirmed.
* Lead Magnet campaigns cannot be activated without a linked resource.
* Existing campaign types are unaffected.
* Focused tests cover UI visibility, context field persistence, activation guard, remove-resource pause behavior, replace-does-not-pause, and non-Lead-Magnet regressions.

relatedSnapshot.title: Campaign duplication copies linked resources
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Objective

When a Lead Magnet campaign is duplicated, copy its linked Hosted Resources independently so the clone does not depend on the original campaign's resource.

## Scope

* Update campaign duplication logic to copy linked Hosted Resources.
* For uploaded files, duplicate the underlying hosted file or storage object into a new Hosted Resource.
* For external URLs, create a new Hosted Resource row with the same URL and metadata.
* Carry over the resource's context/description text to the copied resource.
* Link copied resources to the cloned campaign.
* Preserve resource purpose, such as `lead_magnet`.
* Ensure later changes to one campaign's resource do not affect the other.

## Acceptance Criteria

* Duplicating a Lead Magnet campaign creates linked resources for the clone.
* Uploaded resources are independent hosted files/resources for the clone.
* External URL resources are independent Hosted Resource rows for the clone.
* The clone's resource retains the original's context/description text, independently editable.
* Editing, replacing, or removing the original campaign resource does not affect the clone.
* Editing, replacing, or removing the clone resource does not affect the original.
* Non-Lead-Magnet campaign duplication behavior is unchanged.
* Focused tests cover uploaded resources, external URL resources, context/description copy, independence between original and clone, and non-Lead-Magnet duplication regression.

relatedSnapshot.title: Fix OAuth preview redirect for current Vercel preview domains
relatedSnapshot.description:
Name 2/Outlook OAuth callbacks were not redirecting back to preview deployments because the trusted preview-domain matcher only allowed the legacy *-aiacquisition.vercel.app suffix. Current preview

aliases now use *-acquisity.vercel.app, so the callback treated the preview appOrigin as unverified and fell back to the canonical app URL.

This updates the shared partner preview-domain matcher to support both current and legacy Acquisity Vercel preview suffixes while still rejecting arbitrary *.vercel.app hosts. The fix is applied

consistently across server partner resolution, edge partner resolution, and auth/CORS allowed origins.

Validation includes regression coverage for:

* Current *-acquisity.vercel.app preview URLs
* Legacy *-aiacquisition.vercel.app preview URLs
* Rejection of arbitrary/malformed Vercel hosts
* Name 2 and Outlook OAuth callbacks forwarding back to verified preview origins

relatedSnapshot.title: AI SDR Lead Magnet intent routing + send-resource step
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Objective

Modify AI SDR routing so Lead Magnet campaigns can send the linked Hosted Resource when a prospect shows positive interest but does not explicitly book.

The new AI SDR step should receive the resource URL directly and include it in the reply.

## Scope

* Modify the AI SDR intent router for Lead Magnet campaign types.
* Add a new Lead Magnet send-resource step or agent.
* Run this behavior only when the campaign type is `lead-magnet` and a Lead Magnet Hosted Resource is linked.
* Pass the linked resource's context/description (from ENG-9970 / stored per ENG-9968) into the send-resource step prompt so the reply can speak to what is being sent rather than emitting a blind URL.
* Keep booking intent as the highest-priority route.
* For positive non-booking replies, send the resource.
* For mixed signal replies, send the resource and continue booking.
* When a Lead Magnet campaign routes to booking, book the call type configured in the Lead Magnet Method settings (ENG-10234), falling back to a safe default if unset.
* Leave existing question, objection, negative, out-of-office, wrong-person, referral, and platform-switch routes unchanged.
* Do not add general-purpose `{{magnet}}` merge variable support in this ticket.

## Acceptance Criteria

* Explicit booking intent routes to booking, even on Lead Magnet campaigns.
* Positive non-booking replies on Lead Magnet campaigns trigger the send-resource step.
* Mixed signal replies send the resource and continue into booking behavior.
* The send-resource step receives the resource context/description and the reply reflects it (not a bare URL with no context).

relatedSnapshot.title: fix(website): resolve Vercel deployment URL from aliases instead of project name
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Problem Statement

After publishing a website, Name 13 displays a broken Vercel URL that returns a 404. For example, the displayed URL was `<url:<project-slug>.vercel.app>` (404), while the actual working Vercel URLs were `<url:<project-slug>.vercel.app>` and `<url:<project-slug>.vercel.app>`.

## Impact

* **User Impact**: Users see a broken URL after publishing — clicking it shows a 404 page, even though their site is actually deployed and accessible at a different URL.
* **Business Impact**: Affects any website with a long project name (total DNS label > 63 chars after Vercel appends the team slug).

## Root Cause

The code was constructing the public URL as `<url:${storedprojectname}.vercel.app>`, but Vercel's actual production URL format is `{project-name}-{team-slug}.vercel.app`. Per RFC 1035, DNS labels are capped at 63 characters — so Vercel silently truncates the project-name portion when the combined label is too long.

## Solution

1. Read actual aliases from Vercel API
2. New `resolveVercelProductionUrl` helper picks shortest `.vercel.app` alias
3. Stop constructing URLs from project name
4. Cap project name at 48 chars to prevent future truncation

## Related

* PR: <url:github.com>
* Reported in Slack by Rose: website `<uuid>` showed broken URL after publish

relatedSnapshot.title: Image uploads broken across the app (announcements, workspace logos, avatars, Lead Magnet resources) after images-bucket signing hardening
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Since July 1, uploading images is broken across large parts of the app in production. Admins cannot add images to announcements, workspaces cannot change their logo (confirmed in prod), users cannot change avatars, and the newly launched Lead Magnet campaign type cannot accept resource files at all. This blocks publishing the Lead Magnet launch announcement (it needs screenshots) and blocks the Lead Magnet feature itself.

## Problem

PR #4842 (ENG-10207, merged 2026-07-01, in prod) hardened `uploads.signedUploadUrl` for the shared images bucket. It now requires an `organizationId` on every request plus an organization-scoped upload path. Only the AI chat uploaders were migrated to comply (via the new `useR2Upload` hook). Everything else uploads through `useS3Upload` (`apps/web/hooks/use-s3-upload.ts`), which sends no `organizationId`, so the server rejects the request before an upload URL is issued. Users see generic failure toasts like "Failed to upload media."

**Confirmed broken (all sign against the images bucket via** `useS3Upload`**):**

* Admin announcement images, v1 + v2 editors (`announcement-image-upload.tsx`, `announcement-media-upload.tsx`)
* **Lead Magnet resource uploads** (`campaign-lead-magnet-resource-card.tsx`, path `hosted-resources/{orgId}/...`): launched 2026-07-02, cannot accept files. A Lead Magnet campaign cannot go active without a resource, so the feature is unusable
* Workspace/organization logos (`organization-logo-card.tsx`), confirmed broken in prod by James
* User avatars (`user-avatar-upload.tsx`)
* CRM contact and company avatars
* Brand kit logos and favicons (`brand-identity-card.tsx`)
* Partner branding logos (`logo-upload.tsx`)
* Admin AI tool / AI employee / talent images
* Name 2 manager library uploads (`library-panel.tsx`)

Not affected: chat attachments (migrated by #4842), announcement videos (separate bucket and branch), recordings.

## Solution

Scope the new enforcement to the private path prefixes ENG-10207 actually protects, instead of the whole bucket:

* `apps/web/trpc/routers/uploads.ts`: in `signedUploadUrl` and `signedDownloadUrl`, require `organizationId` + membership + org-scoped path ONLY for private prefixes (`ai-growth-consultant/`, `hosted-resources/`). Keep the path-traversal guard (`isNormalizedObjectPath`) for all images-bucket paths. Other images paths return to the long-standing pre-#4842 rule (any signed-in user can sign), which restores every broken uploader with no client changes.
* `apps/web/hooks/use-s3-upload.ts`: accept and forward an optional `organizationId`.
* `campaign-lead-magnet-resource-card.tsx`: pass `organizationId` so Lead Magnet uploads satisfy the retained `hosted-resources/` protection.
* `deleteObject` is untouched (its strictness predates #4842).

## Scope

* `apps/web/trpc/routers/uploads.ts`
* `apps/web/hooks/use-s3-upload.ts`
* `apps/web/components/campaigns/detail/tabs/options/campaign-lead-magnet-resource-card.tsx`
* `apps/web/tests/trpc/routers/uploads.test.ts`

## Permissions

* Chat-attachment and hosted-resource paths: organization membership required (unchanged from #4842's intent).
* All other images-bucket paths: any authenticated user, matching pre-July-1 behavior.
* Announcement videos: unchanged admin/partner-admin checks.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Admin can upload images in the announcement editor (v1 and v2)
- [ ] Lead Magnet resource card accepts PDF/PNG/JPG uploads and the resource saves
- [ ] Workspace logo, user avatar, CRM avatar, brand kit, partner logo, admin AI tool/employee/talent, and ads library uploads work again
- [ ] Chat attachment uploads still require org membership and org-scoped paths
- [ ] `hosted-resources/{otherOrg}/...` signing with a different org id is rejected
- [ ] Path traversal segments are rejected for all images-bucket signing
- [ ] Unit tests cover the restored bare-path signing and the retained protections

## Open follow-ups

* Per-asset-class upload authorization matrix (admin-only prefixes for announcements/AI tools/talent, self-scoped avatars, partner-scoped branding). Separate hardening ticket after this restore ships.

## Outcome

All image uploads work again, the Lead Magnet feature is usable, ENG-10207's real protection stays intact, and the Lead Magnet launch announcement can be published with screenshots.

relatedSnapshot.title: Dynamic lead magnets via workflows
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Holding note

Create a future implementation ticket/epic for dynamic Lead Magnets via Workflows. This is intentionally a broad backlog placeholder; we will ticket it out properly when we get to building.

Source doc: <url:docs.google.com>

## Concept

When a positive reply comes in on a Lead Magnet campaign, AI SDR pauses before sending the resource, a workflow researches the prospect/company and generates a custom asset, then publishes it as a link and hands it back to AI SDR to send with context.

The static Lead Magnet resource remains the fallback if the workflow fails or times out, so one positive reply sends exactly one magnet: dynamic if ready, static if not.

## Notes from outline

* Depends on the static Lead Magnet work shipping first.
* Adds per-thread magnet override: URL + asset context override the campaign default for that thread.
* Requires SDR hold gate at the send-resource route, not a workflow step that races after SDR starts responding.
* Workflow output should normalize to URL + context for PDFs, images, pages, or pass-through links.
* Possible future pieces: AI SDR Send Lead Magnet workflow step, Host Lead Magnet Asset / Render PDF steps, Name 13 Generate & Publish Page step, dynamic resource mode in campaign setup, template gallery, idempotency, caps, feature flag, playground/dry-run QA.

## Open questions to resolve before implementation

* Workflows GA/timeline dependency.
* Pricing and credit model for workflow/AI/v0 usage.
* Default hold deadline and client-facing fallback behavior.

relatedSnapshot.title: AI SDR email linkifies a URL containing  at  to the bare site root, so shared links point at the wrong page
relatedSnapshot.description: ## Overview Any URL whose path contains an at is turned into a hyperlink to the bare site root in outgoing AI SDR email, with the rest of the address left as plain text after the anchor. YouTube channel handles and LinkedIn profile URLs are the common cases. The email reads correctly but every click lands on the site homepage instead of the intended page. ## Problem The AI SDR shares links such as a podcast channel or a profile as part of answering prospects. Recipients who click are sent to the wrong page, and because the visible text still spells out the full address, neither the operator nor the recipient notices. It was reported to support as "the link for Name 12 is still not showing proper link". ## Root cause apps/web/lib/utils/linkify-html.ts, `linkifyText`: URL_PATTERN's trailing path character class `[-a-zA-Z0-9():%_+.~#?&/=]*` does not include ' at ', so matching stops before the handle. The replacement then builds the anchor from the truncated match, and `linkifyHtml` emits the remainder as ordinary text outside the anchor. For `` the stored result is `>`. Reached on the AI SDR send path from apps/web/lib/ai-sdr-v2/utils/format-email-for-sending.ts, which workflow/steps/send-email.ts, followup-workflow.ts and send-dry-email.ts all call. The same utility also serves the Company Two manual-reply router and the inbox thread view, so those surfaces carry the same defect. ## Blast radius Exact for the signature used, counted 2026-09-16: 6954 sent messages, 218 organizations, 443 users, first occurrence 2025-12-05 and latest 2026-09-16, so it is still occurring. `SELECT count(*) AS messages, count(DISTINCT t.organization_id) AS orgs, min(m.created_at) AS first_seen, max(m.created_at) AS last_seen FROM crm_message m JOIN crm_message_thread t ON t.id = m.thread_id WHERE m.body_html LIKE '% at %' AND m.direction='sent';` The ` at ` shape is the renderer's own output, and a shape audit found about 99.7% of matching rows carry the exact anchor form produced by this code, so this counts the affected set rather than a proxy. It covers sent messages only. Confirmed affected from the report that produced this master: 1 workspace and 1 message. ## Proposed fix The pattern must accept ' at ' in the URL path so the anchor covers the whole URL. The existing behaviour that bare email addresses are not linkified must be preserved, and a URL immediately followed by an email address or a trailing ' at ' must still resolve correctly. ## What's included The linkifier itself and every caller that passes AI SDR or CRM message bodies through it. Not included: any separate rendering defect in the customer's own email client, which the stored body rules out. ## Regression seam apps/web/tests/lib/utils/linkify-html.test.ts. Name 17 `` and a LinkedIn-style `/in/` path must produce an href equal to the full URL with no text left outside the anchor, while the existing cases that assert bare email addresses stay unlinked keep passing. Red before at af923593b4939684f61615429f3649111217a641, green after. ## Done when * A URL containing ' at ' in its path is linkified into a single anchor covering the whole URL. * Bare email addresses remain unlinked. * A regression test proves the behaviour at the linkifier seam. ## Reports * ENG-13948
